_comment: Reviewer-approved divergences between a site's recorded golden SQL and what
the ORM actually emits, per plan 7.2 Layer 1: 'Where the ORM legitimately
emits different-but-equivalent SQL, the reviewer records the approved diff
and a justification in the manifest entry; CI fails on any unapproved
Declarative, like keep-raw.json, so the decision survives manifest
regeneration and is reviewed as a diff rather than hand-edited into the
manifest. Every entry needs a reason: an approved diff is an assertion that
two statements are equivalent, and that assertion has to be justified.
`sql` is the statement the ORM emits. It is compared canonically, so keyword
case, whitespace and identifier quoting do not need to match exactly.

NOTE: LIMIT and OFFSET no longer need entries here. golden.go resolves their bound values back into the render (resolveLimitOffset), which is stricter than an approved diff because it catches a changed limit value.

diffs.sql: INSERT INTO newsfeed_reports (newsfeedid, reason, userid) VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE reason = ?
diffs.reason: GORM emits the columns of a map-valued Create in alphabetical key order, so newsfeedid/reason/userid replaces the handwritten userid/newsfeedid/reason. The bind values are emitted in the same order as the columns, so the row written is identical. Equivalent, not merely similar.

diffs.sql: SELECT msgid FROM messages_pinned WHERE msgid IN (?)
diffs.reason: NOT an ORM artefact - a deliberate code change, recorded here so it is reviewed as one. The original built its IN list by formatting each id with strconv.FormatUint and joining them straight into the SQL text; the conversion binds a []uint64 instead. The rows returned are identical, so this is equivalent in result, but the statement text genuinely differs and plan 7.3 asks for pure no-behaviour-change releases - hence an explicit entry rather than a silent pass. Justified because splicing integers into SQL text is worth removing on its own merits: it defeats the prepared-statement cache (a distinct statement per list length) and it is the shape of an injection bug even where, as here, the ids come from our own rows rather than user input. The adversarial review lists switching these helpers to binds as the sanctioned fix for the literal-int category.

diffs.sql: UPDATE `groups` SET polyindex = ST_GeomFromText(COALESCE(poly, polyofficial, 'POINT(0 0)'), 3857) WHERE id = ?
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - the recorded golden ('...POINT(0 0)'), %d) WHERE id = ?') is unresolved template text, not real SQL: the original spliced utils.SRID into the raw string via fmt.Sprintf BEFORE it ever reached Exec, so the extractor never saw a literal number to record. The conversion moves the same fmt.Sprintf call inside gorm.Expr(...) so GORM sees identical text (utils.SRID is 3857, a fixed Go constant, so this is the only value it can ever produce) - same mechanism already recognised for location.go's locations_spatial REPLACE sites (25b7b92e33fd/6f1d6543e5c0), whose goldens the extractor resolves to the literal 3857 because gorm.Expr(fmt.Sprintf(...)) is the pattern it folds. This site's gorm.Expr call is one level further from the Create(map{...}) call the extractor's fold logic looks for (it is the second argument to .Update(col, value), not a map value), so the same fold did not fire automatically; recorded here rather than left to silently never pass Layer 1.

NOT a behaviour change - same unresolved-template-golden situation as 548090e97d00 (see that entry): the original spliced utils.SRID via fmt.Sprintf before Raw, so the recorded golden's '%d' was never real SQL. The conversion applies the SAME fmt.Sprintf call to the Select(...) string instead (plus group.go's validateGeometry BuildClauses={"SELECT"} technique, site 6d0982e798b5, for the bare-scalar-SELECT shape), producing identical text since utils.SRID is a fixed constant. Recorded because the extractor's fold logic is scoped to gorm.Expr(fmt.Sprintf(...)) specifically and did not fire for a Select(fmt.Sprintf(...), ...) call.

diffs.sql: UPDATE locations SET `type` = 'Polygon', ourgeometry = ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857) WHERE id = ?
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - same unresolved-template-golden situation as 548090e97d00 (see that entry). The conversion's ourgeometry assignment uses the identical gorm.Expr(fmt.Sprintf("ST_GeomFromText(?, %d)", utils.SRID), *req.Polygon) idiom as location.go's locations_spatial REPLACE sites (25b7b92e33fd/6f1d6543e5c0), but as one clause.Set entry's Value rather than a Create(map{...}) value, so the extractor's fold (scoped to the map-Create shape) did not fire. `type` = 'Polygon' is unchanged - a literal in both the original and the conversion (clause.Set's Value is gorm.Expr("'Polygon'"), not a bound Go string), so it never had a placeholder to fold in the first place.

diffs.sql: SELECT ST_AsText(CASE WHEN ourgeometry IS NOT NULL THEN ourgeometry ELSE geometry END) AS old_geometry, CASE WHEN ST_Intersects( CASE WHEN ourgeometry IS NOT NULL THEN ourgeometry ELSE geometry END, ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857)) THEN ST_AsText(ST_UNION( CASE WHEN ourgeometry IS NOT NULL THEN ourgeometry ELSE geometry END, ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857))) ELSE NULL END AS unioned FROM locations WHERE id = ?
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - same unresolved-template-golden situation as round 3's 548090e97d00/745c0a9ca82e/aa63c688e6b1 (see 548090e97d00's approved diff for the full explanation): the recorded golden has a literal '%d' because the original spliced utils.SRID via fmt.Sprintf before Raw. This site was also mislabelled 'Top-level UNION' - ST_UNION() is a geometry function inside one ordinary SELECT with a FROM, not a SQL UNION statement, so no BuildClauses override was needed either, just the same fmt.Sprintf-folded-SRID technique this function's other two sites already use.

diffs.sql: INSERT INTO locations (canon, geometry, name, popularity, type) VALUES (?, ST_GeomFromText(?, 3857), ?, 0, 'Polygon')
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - same unresolved-template-golden situation as 548090e97d00 (see that entry). utils.SRID is a fixed constant (3857), so this is the only value the conversion's gorm.Expr(fmt.Sprintf(...)) can ever produce. Column order is GORM's usual alphabetical map-Create order; normaliseColumnOrder pairs each column with its value regardless of position, so this is recorded in render order for clarity, not because the order itself carries meaning.

diffs.sql: INSERT INTO `groups` (nameshort, namefull, onhere, polyindex, publish, type) VALUES (?, ?, 1, ST_GeomFromText('POINT(0 0)', 3857), 1, ?)
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - same unresolved-template-golden situation as 548090e97d00 (see that entry). utils.SRID is a fixed constant (3857). Column order is GORM's usual alphabetical map-Create order; normaliseColumnOrder pairs each column with its value regardless of position.

diffs.sql: SELECT u.id, u.fullname AS name, (SELECT e.email FROM users_emails e WHERE e.userid = u.id AND e.preferred = 1 LIMIT 1) AS email FROM users u WHERE u.id IN (?)
diffs.reason: NOT a behaviour change - the ids were formatted as decimal text and joined directly into the SQL string (same shape markPinned had before it was switched to a bind, site 032b7f1b9500), so the extractor recorded the runtime-built fragment as an unresolved '{{expr}}' rather than any comparable SQL. The conversion binds a []uint64 instead - collapseInLists normalises the semantic 'IN (?)' recorded here against whatever length the rendered 'IN (?,?,...)' actually is, same as any other clean IN-list.

LIMIT 1), 0) AS groupid, COALESCE((SELECT m2.groupid FROM memberships m2 WHERE m2.userid = cm.userid AND m2.groupid IN (?) LIMIT 1), 0) AS groupidfrom FROM chat_messages cm INNER JOIN chat_rooms cr ON cr.id = cm.chatid INNER JOIN users ON users.id = cm.userid AND users.deleted IS NULL LEFT JOIN chat_images ci ON ci.chatmsgid = cm.id LEFT JOIN chat_messages_held cmh ON cmh.msgid = cm.id LEFT JOIN chat_messages_byemail cme ON cme.chatmsgid = cm.id WHERE cm.reviewrequired = 1 AND cm.reviewrejected = 0 AND ( (cr.chattype = ? AND cr.groupid IN (?)) OR (cr.chattype = ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END AND groupid IN (?))) OR (cr.chattype = ? AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = cm.userid AND groupid IN (?)))) GROUP BY cm.id ORDER BY cm.id ASC LIMIT ?
diffs.reason: DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE alongside the ORM conversion, same category as 62a2f6fa4bdb and 032b7f1b9500 (see those entries) - flagged explicitly because most entries in this file record a rendering artefact instead. baseQuery spliced its group-id list as literal comma-joined decimal text five times (four here, a fifth shared with 1ff296c8656c's widerQuery below); the conversion binds a []uint64 (groupIDs) instead, at every occurrence. The extractor recorded this site's goldenSql as an unresolved '{{expr}}' because baseQuery is itself a Go string variable assembled across several statements before reaching db.Raw, not because of the group-id splice specifically - so there was no golden text to diverge from in the usual sense, only an opaque placeholder to replace with the real statement, recorded here. collapseInLists normalises the semantic 'IN (?)' recorded here against whatever length the rendered 'IN (?,?,...)' actually is. groupIDs is always the calling moderator's own memberships (never external input), so this was not an exploitable injection in practice, but removing a literal-int-splice pattern from a moderator-facing query is worth doing on its own merits, same reasoning as 032b7f1b9500. Also has a Layer 2 result-parity test (TestLayer2_5da587b4234d, test/orm_reviewqueue_test.go) given the query's size and the manifest's own recommendation for more scrutiny than a mechanical toggle.

AND cr.groupid IN (?)) OR (cr.chattype = ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END AND groupid IN (?))) OR (cr.chattype = ? AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships WHERE userid = cm.userid AND groupid IN (?)))) UNION SELECT DISTINCT cm.id, cm.chatid, cm.userid, cm.type, cm.message, cm.date, cm.refmsgid, cm.reportreason, cm.imageid, COALESCE(ci.archived, 0) AS image_archived, COALESCE(ci.externaluid, '') AS imageuid, ci.externalmods AS imagemods, cr.chattype AS room_chattype, cr.user1 AS room_user1, cr.user2 AS room_user2, COALESCE(cr.groupid, 0) AS room_groupid, 1 AS widerchatreview, COALESCE(cmh.userid, 0) AS held_by, cmh.timestamp AS held_timestamp, cme.msgid, m1.groupid AS groupid, COALESCE(m2.groupid, 0) AS groupidfrom FROM chat_messages cm INNER JOIN chat_rooms cr ON cr.id = cm.chatid AND cm.reviewrequired = 1 AND cm.reviewrejected = 0 INNER JOIN memberships m1 ON m1.userid = (CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END) INNER JOIN `groups` g ON m1.groupid = g.id AND g.type = 'Freegle' INNER JOIN users ON users.id = cm.userid AND users.deleted IS NULL LEFT JOIN memberships m2 ON m2.userid = cm.userid LEFT JOIN chat_images ci ON ci.chatmsgid = cm.id LEFT JOIN chat_messages_held cmh ON cmh.msgid = cm.id LEFT JOIN chat_messages_byemail cme ON cme.chatmsgid = cm.id WHERE JSON_EXTRACT(g.settings, '$.widerchatreview') = 1 AND cmh.id IS NULL AND (cm.reportreason IS NULL OR cm.reportreason != 'User') AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM memberships m_check WHERE m_check.userid = (CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 THEN cr.user2 ELSE cr.user1 END) AND m_check.groupid IN (?))) combined GROUP BY id ORDER BY widerchatreview ASC, id ASC LIMIT ?
diffs.reason: DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE alongside the ORM conversion - the wider-review twin of 5da587b4234d, sharing baseQuery (see that entry for the group-id-splice-to-bind reasoning, which applies identically here) plus one more occurrence in widerQuery's own NOT EXISTS clause. recipientExpr (the CASE WHEN cm.userid = cr.user1 ... END fragment reused across both queries) needed no change - it is already a fixed Go string constant, not user input; the extractor's inability to const-fold it across the function was a goldenSql-capture limitation, not a real blocker, and is moot once db.Raw is replaced. Top-level UNION wrapped in a derived table with a trailing GROUP BY/ORDER BY/LIMIT that applies to the combined result - same db.Table(...).Select(wholeStatementText).Statement.BuildClauses = []string{"SELECT"} mechanism this file's 33ad97a3417c already uses, and modconfig.go's e9ea468dab80 uses for the same 'ORDER BY belongs to the whole union' shape. Also has a Layer 2 result-parity test (TestLayer2_1ff296c8656c, test/orm_reviewqueue_test.go): this is a large correlated-subquery UNION and the manifest's own keep-raw reason specifically asked for more scrutiny than Layer 1 text-match alone before converting it.

diffs.sql: INSERT INTO trysts (user1, user2, arrangedfor) VALUES (?, ?, ?) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE id = LAST_INSERT_ID(id), arrangedat = NOW()
diffs.reason: DELIBERATE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, not a rendering artefact - flagged explicitly because every other entry in this file records the latter. The golden is the statement as it really was, and it was buggy: the ODKU clause set only arrangedat = NOW(), with no id = LAST_INSERT_ID(id) forcing. MySQL only reports an id on a duplicate-key update when the update assigns it, so on a duplicate hit sqlResult.LastInsertId() returned 0 - and CreateTryst returns that value straight to the caller as {"id": 0}. The unique key arrangedfor_2 (arrangedfor, user1, user2) makes the duplicate path reachable whenever a caller re-arranges the same tryst, so this was live, not theoretical. The approved divergence is the added id = LAST_INSERT_ID(id), which is the idiom the other ten LAST_INSERT_ID sites in this codebase already use. Verified at the database level before and after: unfixed, the second insert of the same pair returns 0; fixed, it returns the same non-zero id as the first. TestCreateTrystDuplicateReturnsExistingID pins that through the HTTP handler. A mechanical port would have reproduced the defect faithfully, which is why it was recorded as the blocker for keeping this site raw - fixing it was the better answer than preserving it.
